guideline_matches.title: Synthetic renal laboratory context checklist (demo v1)
guideline_matches.text: A creatinine result flagged high may be relevant to clinician review of an active antibiotic prescription. Preserve the value, unit, collection date, and laboratory flag. A single creatinine value does not establish a new diagnosis or a trend. Baseline renal measurements, timing, and other relevant context may be missing. Identify these gaps explicitly; do not calculate an unsupported renal estimate or recommend a medication dose adjustment.

guideline_matches.title: Synthetic medication and allergy context checklist (demo v1)
guideline_matches.text: For a synthetic microbiology review, active antibiotic prescriptions may be relevant context. Report the recorded drug, dose, route, frequency, and status exactly as supplied by the medication tool. A prescription record does not establish administration, adherence, indication, or clinical response. A susceptibility result describes an isolate and does not independently establish that a prescription is appropriate or inappropriate. Leave treatment decisions to the clinician.

guideline_matches.title: Synthetic urine culture review checklist (demo v1)
guideline_matches.text: An Escherichia coli (E. coli) urine culture records a laboratory observation. Culture growth alone does not establish symptomatic infection or a need for antibiotics. A reviewer needs symptoms, specimen collection context, and the reason testing was obtained. If these details were not returned by patient tools, list them as missing information. Preserve the specimen, collection date, organism, quantity, and reported qualifiers without inventing additional context.
